<section>Chapter 30. "V" Standard Extension for Vector Operations, Version 1.0 > 30.6. Configuration-Setting Instructions (** **`vsetvli` /** **`vsetivli` /** **`vsetvl` ) > 30.6.3. Constraints on Setting** **`vl`</section>

<target>### **30.6.3. Constraints on Setting** **`vl`**

The `vset{i}vl{i}` instructions first set VLMAX according to their `vtype` argument, then set `vl` obeying the following constraints:

1. `vl = AVL` if `AVL ≤ VLMAX`

2. `ceil(AVL / 2) ≤ vl ≤ VLMAX` if `AVL < (2 * VLMAX)`

3. `vl = VLMAX` if `AVL ≥ (2 * VLMAX)`

4. Deterministic on any given implementation for same input AVL and VLMAX values

5. These specific properties follow from the prior rules:

a. `vl = 0` if `AVL = 0`

b. `vl > 0` if `AVL > 0`

c. `vl ≤ VLMAX`

d. `vl ≤ AVL`

e. a value read from `vl` when used as the AVL argument to `vset{i}vl{i}` results in the same value in `vl` , provided the resultant VLMAX equals the value of VLMAX at the time that `vl` was read



_The_ `vl` _setting rules are designed to be sufficiently strict to preserve_ `vl` _behavior_

_across register spills and context swaps for_ `AVL ≤ VLMAX` _, yet flexible enough to enable implementations to improve vector lane utilization for_ `AVL > VLMAX` _._

_For example, this permits an implementation to set_ `vl = ceil(AVL / 2)` _for_ `VLMAX < AVL < 2*VLMAX` _in order to evenly distribute work over the last two iterations of a stripmine loop. Requirement 2 ensures that the first stripmine iteration of reduction loops uses the largest vector length of all iterations, even in the case of_ `AVL < 2*VLMAX` _. This allows software to avoid needing to explicitly calculate a running maximum of vector lengths observed during a stripmined loop. Requirement 2 also allows an implementation to set vl to VLMAX for_ `VLMAX < AVL < 2*VLMAX`</target>
